description:
Academic CV for PhD Applications: Structure + Example

Direct answer box (first 50 words):

An academic CV for a PhD application is a 2–3 page document that puts your research front and centre: education, research experience, publications, skills and references — in that logic. It is not a job CV. Cut the retail jobs and personality adjectives, and give every line to evidence that you can do research.

What makes a PhD CV different from a job CV

Recruiters want reliability. Supervisors want research potential. That single difference should reshape the whole document:

Job CVAcademic CV for PhD
1 page, always2–3 pages is normal (2 is plenty pre-PhD)
Work experience firstEducation and research first
Buzzwords: "team player", "go-getter"Facts: projects, methods, tools, outputs
Designed to pass ATS filtersRead by a human academic — keep it plain
Interests section expectedOnly include interests if genuinely relevant

Admissions panels and supervisors typically spend 60–90 seconds on a first read. Your CV's only job in that window is to answer three questions: Can this person handle the degree? Have they done anything research-like before? Do they fit my project? Everything else is decoration.

The correct structure (in order)

  1. Name and contact details. University email if you have one, plus a professional personal address. No date of birth, photo or full home address for UK applications.
  2. Education. Reverse chronological. Degree, institution, dates, classification or GPA, and — importantly — your dissertation title. A relevant dissertation is often the strongest research signal a pre-PhD applicant has. List notable modules or rankings only if impressive.
  3. Research experience. Projects, dissertations, lab work, research assistantships. For each: dates, project title, one or two lines on what you did — methods, data, tools — and any outcome (report, grade, presentation, dataset).
  4. Publications and conference papers. Full citations, your name bolded. Preprints, under-review manuscripts and posters all belong here, clearly labelled. If you have none, omit the section entirely — see our guide to starting a PhD without publications; most European positions do not expect them.
  5. Awards, scholarships, funding. Anything competitive, with the year and the selection basis if it was selective.
  6. Teaching, volunteering and relevant work. Demonstrating, tutoring, or work that used your discipline. Bar work goes unless it paid for something relevant.
  7. Technical skills. Programming languages, lab techniques, statistical software, languages. Be specific: "Python (pandas, scikit-learn)" beats "coding".
  8. References. Two academics with name, title, institution and email. Ask them first — see our recommendation letter request templates.

Sample academic CV layout (copy and adapt)

``` JANE OKAFOR j.okafor@university.ac.uk · +44 7xxx xxx xxx · linkedin.com/in/janeokafor

EDUCATION MSc Environmental Science, University of Leeds — 2024–2025 (expected Distinction) Dissertation: "Peatland carbon flux modelling under alternative rewetting scenarios" (supervised by Dr A. Whitfield) BSc Geography, University of Ibadan — 2019–2023 (First Class, GPA 4.5/5.0) Final-year project: flood-risk mapping of the Ogun River basin

RESEARCH EXPERIENCE Research Assistant, Leeds Ecosystem Group — Jun 2025–present Processed two years of eddy-covariance data (Python); co-authored a manuscript on methane flux variability (in preparation). Undergraduate thesis, Ibadan — 2022–2023 Built a GIS flood model (QGIS, R); findings presented at the Nigerian Geographers' Conference 2023 (poster).

PUBLICATIONS Okafor, J. & Adeyemi, T. (2024). Flood-risk mapping of the Ogun River basin. Journal of Nigerian Geoscience, 12(2), 45–58.

AWARDS Commonwealth Shared Scholarship shortlist, 2024 · Dean's Prize, Best Graduating Student, Geography, 2023

SKILLS Python (pandas, scikit-learn) · R · QGIS · eddy-covariance processing · French (B1)

REFERENCES Dr A. Whitfield, Associate Professor, University of Leeds — a.whitfield@... Prof. T. Adeyemi, University of Ibadan — t.adeyemi@... ```

That is roughly what a competitive applicant's CV looks like. Notice what it does not contain: objectives, photos, secondary school, soft-skill word clouds.

Tailoring the CV to each application

For advertised PhD positions, spend 20 minutes per application reordering and rewording:

  • Mirror the methods and keywords from the advert in your skills and project descriptions. Our guide to reading a PhD job advert properly shows how to extract them.
  • Move the research experience most relevant to the project to the top of its section.
  • Adjust the dissertation line to emphasise the subfield the supervisor works in.
  • For self-proposed projects, your CV should visibly support your proposal — the methods you list should match the methods your research proposal promises.

Mistakes that cost interviews

  • Padding with irrelevance. Five years of hospitality jobs listed in detail signals you had nothing else to show, not diligence.
  • Vague project descriptions. "Worked on machine learning" tells a supervisor nothing. "Built a CNN classifier reaching 84% F1 on a 10k-image dataset" does.
  • Missing dates or gaps left unexplained. If you have a gap, handle it briefly and honestly — our academic gap guide covers wording that works.
  • Design over substance. Columns, icons and colours mostly waste space. Plain, single-column, generous white space wins.
  • Exceeding 3 pages. If you have not yet done a PhD, you do not need 3 pages.

Formatting rules that quietly matter

  • One font (Calibri, Cambria or Times), 10.5–11pt body, single column.
  • PDF only, named Surname-Firstname-CV.pdf.
  • Consistent date format throughout ("Sep 2023 – Jun 2025").
  • Bullet points for anything beyond one line; no paragraphs.
  • Save the plain-text master somewhere you can update per application without starting over.

Pair the CV with a short, specific cover letter — our PhD cover letter sample shows the structure. The CV proves capability; the letter proves fit.

Frequently asked questions

How long should an academic CV be for a PhD application? Two pages is ideal for most pre-PhD applicants; three is acceptable with a Master's, publications or substantial research work. One page is fine early on — never pad to fill space.

Should I include my photo or date of birth? No for UK, Irish and US applications. In Germany and some other European countries a photo is still conventional but optional — omitting it will not harm you anywhere.

Do I list my high school? No, unless you are applying straight from secondary school with essentially no university record yet. Otherwise, your degree makes it redundant.

What if I have no research experience at all? Then your dissertation, final-year project and any data-heavy coursework carry the CV. Frame them rigorously: research question, method, dataset, result. That framing is what panels read as research experience.
